newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends down on firmer peso.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends down on firmer peso.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates closed down 25 basis points at 23.25 percent due to a firm peso and lower U.S. long bond yields, after what traders said was a calm session.
"The peso was very firm, and in fact moved much more than secondary rates, but did much to help them nonetheless," a trader said.
Benchmark 48-hour contracts ended down 4.7 centavos at 7.8950/7.8990 per dollar. U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds were meanwhile up 20/32 in late trade, to yield 7.07 percent.
Dealers noted that overnight Cetes rates had pared an earlier fall of 50 basis points due to forecasts that domestic primary interest rates would increase again this week. "The
peso should have brought government secondary rates down far," another trader said. "But it did not have that influence precisely because of the primary auction outlook."
Traders said rates on bellwether 28-day Cetes could gain by up to 100 basis points from a current level of 21.86 percent at Tuesday night's primary auction of government securities.
Other traders said overnight rates declined on foreign demand for paper.
Banco de Mexico drained 4.344 billion pesos from the market through five secondary auctions which it assigned at rates of between 24.70-25.29 percent.
Overnight rates on bank paper closed down 65 basis points at 24.75 percent.
Liquidity of 2.759 billion pesos was slated to return to the system on Tuesday from prior central bank participation.
